headline: Highest risk is low: no shared execution or data channel is documented, so prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors are largely blocked by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no documented filesystem, MCP, browser, or subprocess surfaces, and Superset only exposes an API with allowlisted egress. With no shared channel or ingestion path documented, there is no plausible default prompt-injection bridge between the pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected through a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge, reassess injection risk.
IF Superset begins parsing LightZero output as instructions, the pathway changes materially.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate hosts or containers.
Do not add a shared workspace or clipboard bridge.
Disable any future MCP connector between them unless provenance checks are added.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows sensitive data classes, shared workspace, or unrestricted egress. LightZero has no filesystem read/write, and Superset only has allowlisted network egress, so there is no documented path for one agent to leak the other's data by default.
conditions: IF either agent is given access to PHI, secrets, or a shared workspace, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF Superset is configured to ingest files from LightZero outputs, the data-flow assumption no longer holds.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
Keep Superset API credentials separate from LightZero runtime.
Review outbound allowlists before enabling any new connector.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, while Superset only documents allowlisted egress and API calls. Because neither agent has overlapping mutable write authority in the profiles, capability conflict is not plausible here.
conditions: IF LightZero gains write access to the same directory or git repo as Superset, conflict risk appears.
IF Superset is extended with filesystem or git write capabilities, reassess for race conditions.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only relative to shared artifacts.
Add file locks before any future shared-write workflow.

D_cascading_error.rationale: The profiles do not document a pipeline where Superset consumes LightZero outputs as authoritative input, nor any downstream action-taking authority. Without a documented handoff, there is no default cascade from LightZero's game-playing outputs into Superset actions.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are wired into Superset dashboards or automation without validation, cascading error risk increases.
IF Superset begins acting on LightZero-generated facts, add verification gates.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any downstream action.
Require schema validation on any exchanged output.
Log and diff all handoffs between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both profiles are open-source with empty touched-data fields. Because the compliance pathway is not evidenced, no specific residency or retention mismatch can be asserted.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent, compliance must be reassessed.
IF either deployment adds residency or retention constraints, compare them before pairing.
mitigations: Document the data classes each agent may process.
Keep regulated data out of this pair until controls are defined.
